newsitem.title: JAPAN: Economists expect no change in BOJ bond buying.
newsitem.headline: Economists expect no change in BOJ bond buying.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) has little reason to reduce the amount of its outright bond purchases now, but the central bank may consider it in the future if bank note growth slows, economists said on Monday.
The BOJ offered to buy 100 billion yen worth of JGBs outright on Monday morning, providing relief to the Japanese government bond (JGB) market.
There had been widespread speculation since last week that the BOJ may reduce the number of its outright bond-buying operations, one of the key supportive factors for the JGB market, to once a month.
The BOJ currently conducts outright JGB purchase operations twice a month, buying 100 billion yen each time.
A BOJ official said he would not comment about today's outright bond purchase.

"The BOJ reduced the amount of outright bond purchases late last year due to a slowdown in bank note growth. However, it has no reason now to further reduce bond buying as bank notes have been maintaining a year-on-year growth of around eight percent," said Yasunari Ueno, chief market economist at Fuji Securities.

The BOJ surprised the JGB market in December 1996 by reducing the amount of its outright bond purchase to 100 billion yen. Until then, the central bank had been buying 200 billion yen worth on each occasion.
A slowdown in bank note growth during the October-December quarter 1996 had been cited by economists as the reason behind the BOJ's decision.
The average amount of bank notes outstanding in October-December 1996 rose 7.9 percent year-on-year. This compares with growth of 10.0 percent in April-June and 9.0 percent in July-September.

During the first three months of 1997, bank note growth has shown little deviation from the October-December trend. The data for April will be released on Thursday. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
